Catalogue / NeuroMusic

NeuroMusic

Live Music & Neuroscience

Booking enquiry

Live performances informed by neuroscience research

NeuroMusic explores the connection between music, the mind and the way we listen. Bringing live performance into dialogue with neuroscience, the project invites a deeper awareness of mental wellbeing, hearing and our everyday sound environment.

The founders

Yury & Elena Revich

Brother and sister. Violinists. Heirs to a musical tradition spanning for more than four generations.

Co-founder & Artistic Director

Yury Revich

Stradivari violinist, composer,
ECHO Klassik and ICMA winner

Yury has performed at Carnegie Hall, the Vienna Musikverein and
La Scala, with recordings featured in Netflix’s Bridgerton
Founder of Festival Nights and Honorary Representative of
UNICEF Austria, he brings together music,
visual art and social initiatives

Co-founder

Elena Revich

Violinist, diploma winner of
the International Tchaikovsky Competition

Elena is an internationally acclaimed violinist and the author of interdisciplinary projects that have received prestigious awards, including the Golden Mask
Elena developed the NeuroMusic approach in dialogue with neuroscientists, exploring how music shapes perception, emotion and attention

Live music, visual art
and neuroscience

Visual artist

Tatiana Plakhova

Complexity Graphics ↗

NeuroMusic was developed with the participation of the internationally renowned visual artist Tatiana Plakhova.

Her visuals accompany the live performance and follow the programme from state to state, giving each listening state and the research behind it its own visual language.

Catalogue/VitaDuo

VitaDuo

International Chamber Duo
Saxophone & Piano
Booking enquiry Request press kit
About

Pianist Maria Nemtsova and saxophonist Vitaly Vatulya perform together as VitaDuo, exploring new music and arrangements for saxophone and piano.

Their performances have taken them to more than 50 cities, including Moscow, Tel Aviv, Prague, Tbilisi, Vienna and Belgrade, and to festivals such as Slavic Spring in Prague, SaxArte in Italy and Autumn in Carthage in Tunis.

They also co-founded Music for Peace, a charitable project that brings concerts and masterclasses to communities affected by conflict and supports young musicians in these regions.

Catalogue/Amstel Quartet

Amstel Quartet

Amsterdam-based Saxophone Quartet The most colourful saxophone quartet in the world
Booking enquiry
{{ v }}✦
{{ m.n }} {{ m.voice }} {{ m.name }}

{{ p }}

Over 25 years, Amstel Quartet has set a new standard for the saxophone quartet and explored the instrument across its full range.

The quartet has an unmistakable group sound that combines virtuosity with deep musicality and expressiveness. Alongside adventurous repertoire, it works closely with contemporary composers to create new music for saxophone quartet. Amstel Quartet has performed at the Concertgebouw in Amsterdam and Carnegie Hall in New York, and has toured Europe, the UK, Russia, the Middle East, China, Japan, Canada and the United States.
